ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as not upheld: the surge rise from 1× to 1.4× was notified in-app at 12:01:40, before the 12:02:00 trip start, with all three SURGE-1 items stated, so the $27.82 fare stands and no refund is issued. ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a fare/surge dispute: the rider was quoted $21.67 at surge 1× (F6) and charged $27.82 at surge 1.4× from trip start (F5, F7), so the fare exceeds the quote by $6.15 (F8); the whole difference comes from the multiplier change, because the billed distance of 8.63 km sits under the 8.7 km optimal route (F3) and there is no off-route segment — no RD-1/RD-2 excess-distance refund arises (F1).

SURGE-1 is satisfied. The trace marks the rise (1× → 1.4×) and the in-app notification at or before pickup as settled ✓ (F8, F9). Reading the logged notice text itself — "Fares are 1.4× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $29.75. You can cancel for free." — it states the new multiplier (1.4×), a revised estimated fare ($29.75) and free cancellation without penalty; all three SURGE-1 items are present (F9). The rider's complaint that the notice "only popped up as I was getting into the car" is a statement contradicted by the platform's timestamped surge log, which places it at 12:01:40, 20 seconds before trip start at 12:02:00 (F2, F9); the system record governs that conflict [SURGE-1]. The fact that the stated estimate ($29.75) exceeded the fare finally charged ($27.82) does not make the notice deficient: SURGE-1 requires a revised estimated fare to be stated, and no item is vague or contradicted within the notice itself [SURGE-1].

Because the rider was notified, SURGE-2's "rider not notified → refund the surge differential" row is not triggered; the higher fare stands [SURGE-2]. The differential arithmetic — "(1.4 − 1.0) × $18.82 = $7.53, capped at the $6.15 the fare exceeds the quote" (F8) — is therefore never payable [SURGE-3]. The chat contains only pickup logistics with no fare or route agreement (F10, F11) and is complete and timestamped (F12), and the driver states he followed the app's route (F13), which the GPS record supports.

Safety screen: I read both chat messages (caller at the taxi stand in a red cap; driver arriving in a black Hyundai Ioniq), the driver's post-trip statement, the rider's complaint and both briefs. Nothing describes threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks, dangerous driving or an accident; the complaint is about notice timing only. No safety basis exists.

Evidence: the surge log with timestamp and quoted text (F9), the fare build-up (F5, F7, F8) and the complete timestamped chat (F12) settle every element this ruling needs, so the record is sufficient. The amount in issue, $6.15, is under $10, within the system's final jurisdiction under TH-1/TH-2 (C1).

Precedent: DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice) supports a refund only where notice was missing; here the notice was given, so the fare stands.
